description: Server-side Minecraft zombie apocalypse mod with configurable waves, hordes, blood moons, progression, siege behavior, and mod compatibility.

mods.name: Zombie Apocalypse Addon
mods.description:
A server-side configurable zombie apocalypse gameplay addon for NeoForge 1.21.1.

Install this on the server. Clients do not need the mod to join.

Start with /za for a short dashboard, safe presets, and config help.

Core gameplay:
- Optional sunlight immunity for zombies.
- Custom day/night spawning near players.
- Optional zombie block breaking, block placing, and swarm towering.
- Horde events and blood moon nights.
- Day-based difficulty scaling.
- Death cooldown safety window.
- Persistent kill and cooldown statistics.

Use /za help for topic-based command help. Existing detailed commands remain available.

releases.notes:
## Changes

- Better fresh-install defaults. The first day (day 0) is now safe in daylight so players can gather gear; nights are not. Scheduled hordes now arrive at dusk and last about the whole night (10 minutes) instead of starting at dawn for 5 minutes. Existing configs keep their values; run `/za preset standard` to switch to the new balance.
- Presets now set hordes to arrive at dusk, and their horde lengths cover the night: Casual 6 minutes, Standard 10, Hardcore 12. Casual now protects every lit area like Standard does.
- `/za day` shows the time as a clock with the phase, for example `19:30 (night)`, and warns that vanilla `/time set` resets the day counter.

## Fixes

- Forge and NeoForge 1.20.1: an in-game change made while the config file was missing lines no longer writes defaults for those lines, and a hand edit picked up by an in-game change is now announced to operators like other file edits.
- The `[compatibility]` section comment pointed at `/za compatibility on` for restoring safeguards; it now points at `/za config reset compatibility`.

## Documentation

- New wiki pages: a Config Reference with every setting, its default, allowed range, and description, generated from the mod, and an FAQ.
- The README, descriptions, and wiki now list exactly what a fresh install does and compare the three presets value by value.

## Files

- `zombieapocalypseaddon-2.8.0.jar` - NeoForge 1.21.1 (NeoForge 21.1.218+, Java 21)
- `zombieapocalypseaddon-neoforge-1.20.1-1.11.0.jar` - NeoForge 1.20.1 (Java 17)
- `zombieapocalypseaddon-forge-1.20.1-1.11.0.jar` - Forge 1.20.1 (Forge 47.4.18+, Java 17)

releases.notes:
This release is about settings staying the way you set them.

## Changes

- Feature `on` commands no longer load presets. `/za events on`, `/za bloodmoon on`, `/za breaking on`, `/za placing on`, `/za towering on`, `/za scaling on`, `/za spawn on`, `/za attributes on`, `/za compatibility on`, the `/za spawn <feature> on` switches, and every `enabled on` form used to overwrite the whole section, and some also reset the main spawn settings such as spawn chance, range, and light protection. Now they only turn the feature on, turn on a switch it depends on, and fix a value that would leave it doing nothing (like a 0% chance). The reply lists every extra change.
- Features with a start day now wait for it when turned on, and the reply says when they start. `dayone` turns the feature on and starts it today.
- `/za towering unlimited` only changes the cap settings it is named for.
- `/za spawn daytime on` no longer resets `daylightSpawnStartDay`.

## Features

- `/za config reset <section>` puts one config section back to its defaults, and `/za config reset all` resets everything. Tab completion lists the sections.
- Operators now get a chat message when edits to the config file are applied, listing what changed.

## Fixes

- Forge and NeoForge 1.20.1: edits to the config file made while the server runs are now applied reliably. The loader's file watcher skipped most normal saves, so edits were often ignored until later. The mod now watches its own file, applies an edit once the save has finished, and never applies a file that does not parse or is missing settings.
- Forge and NeoForge 1.20.1: saving the file while the loader was reading it could reset every setting to its default. In-game changes are now written in one step, and half-written files are ignored.
- NeoForge 1.21.1: an in-game change could undo a file edit that NeoForge had not reloaded yet. Edits on disk are now picked up before every save.
- NeoForge 1.21.1: if the loader resets settings to defaults (after a half-saved read or a typo in the file), the mod puts the previous values back within a couple of seconds and tells operators. For that short moment the defaults are in use.
- A config file with a syntax error no longer breaks in-game changes on 1.20.1 with an unexplained error; the command says what is wrong.

If your settings were reset by an older version, the loader's `zombieapocalypseaddon-common-N.toml.bak` files in the `config` folder hold earlier copies.

## Files

- `zombieapocalypseaddon-2.7.0.jar` - NeoForge 1.21.1 (NeoForge 21.1.218+, Java 21)
- `zombieapocalypseaddon-neoforge-1.20.1-1.10.0.jar` - NeoForge 1.20.1 (Java 17)
- `zombieapocalypseaddon-forge-1.20.1-1.10.0.jar` - Forge 1.20.1 (Forge 47.4.18+, Java 17)

releases.notes:
## Features

- Siege nights: block breaking, block placing, and towering each have a new `events` option (`/za breaking events on`, or `zombieBlockBreakingDuringEvents` and its placing and towering versions). When it is on, zombies can use that ability during hordes and blood moons before its start day, then all the time once the start day is reached. With a start day of 50, zombies only break and build on event nights until day 50.
- Stepped difficulty: `/za scaling steps <days>` (`scalingStepDays`) makes zombie strength rise in jumps instead of a little every day. With `10`, it rises on days 11, 21, 31, and so on, the morning after each 10-day horde.
- Bigger waves over time: `/za scaling extrazombies <count>` (`maxExtraZombiesPerWave`) adds up to that many zombies to every custom wave at full strength, including horde and blood moon waves. It grows with the scaling strength.
- The breaking, placing, and towering dashboards now show whether the feature is active right now and whether it also runs during events. The scaling dashboard shows when strength rises next and the current extra wave size.

All new settings default to off, so existing worlds play the same until you change them.

## Siege night setup

A horde at nightfall every 10th day, breaking and building only on those nights until day 50, and stronger, bigger waves after each one:

```
/za events on
/za events interval 10
/za events chance 1
/za events dusk on
/za events duration 10
/za scaling steps 10
/za scaling extrazombies 4
/za breaking on
/za breaking startday 50
/za breaking events on
/za placing on
/za placing startday 50
/za placing events on
```

Blood moons count as event nights too; use `/za bloodmoon off` if only the scheduled sieges should allow breaking and building.

## Files

- `zombieapocalypseaddon-2.6.0.jar` - NeoForge 1.21.1 (NeoForge 21.1.218+, Java 21)
- `zombieapocalypseaddon-neoforge-1.20.1-1.9.0.jar` - NeoForge 1.20.1 (Java 17)
- `zombieapocalypseaddon-forge-1.20.1-1.9.0.jar` - Forge 1.20.1 (Forge 47.4.18+, Java 17)

releases.notes:
## Fixes

- Changing settings in game on Forge and NeoForge 1.20.1 no longer risks resetting other settings to their defaults. A save could overlap the loader's own config reload, which then "corrected" whole sections such as block breaking or spawning back to defaults and left `.bak` copies in the config folder. Changes are now written to the file and read back from a complete copy, so other settings stay as you set them.

NeoForge 1.21.1 is not affected and stays on 2.5.0.

## Files

- `zombieapocalypseaddon-neoforge-1.20.1-1.8.1.jar` - NeoForge 1.20.1 (Java 17)
- `zombieapocalypseaddon-forge-1.20.1-1.8.1.jar` - Forge 1.20.1 (Forge 47.4.18+, Java 17)

releases.notes:
## Features

- Zombie gear can now come from any mod. Scaled zombies draw armor and weapons from four tiers, `tier1Gear` to `tier4Gear` in `[scaling]`, which start with the same vanilla gear as before. Tier 1 is the most common on early days, and later days favor tiers 3 and 4.
- Each item's slot is detected automatically: helmets go on the head, boots on the feet, and swords, axes, lances, or other items in the main hand. Shields, offhand items, and animal armor are never used. Listing an item twice makes it twice as likely, IDs from mods that are not installed are skipped, and an empty tier falls back to its vanilla gear.
- Added `/za gear` (`/zgear`): a dashboard with today's tier odds, plus `list`, `add` (the item in your hand, or any item ID with tab completion), `remove`, `clear`, `reset`, and `preview`, which spawns a zombie wearing a tier. `/za help gear` shows examples.
- Added `gearDropChance` (`/za gear dropchance`), the chance each piece of addon-given gear drops when a player kills the zombie. The default `0.085` keeps the vanilla rate.

## Fixes

- Bare family commands such as `/za spawn`, `/za events`, `/za scaling`, `/za stats`, and `/za hunt`, plus `/zombieapocalypse`, now open their dashboards instead of reporting an incomplete command.

## Files

- `zombieapocalypseaddon-2.5.0.jar` - NeoForge 1.21.1 (NeoForge 21.1.218+, Java 21)
- `zombieapocalypseaddon-neoforge-1.20.1-1.8.0.jar` - NeoForge 1.20.1 (Java 17)
- `zombieapocalypseaddon-forge-1.20.1-1.8.0.jar` - Forge 1.20.1 (Forge 47.4.18+, Java 17)
